'''Porur''' ({{IPA|ta|poːɾuːɾ|lang}}) is a [[neighbourhood]] of the city of [[Chennai]], [[India]]. It forms part of the [[Maduravoyal taluk]] of [[Chennai district]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-06-10|title=Corporation of Chennai|url=http://www.chennaicorporation.gov.in/images/MAP_ZONE_WARD.jpg|url-status=live|access-date=2021-07-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200610135005/http://www.chennaicorporation.gov.in/images/MAP_ZONE_WARD.jpg|archive-date=2020-06-10}}</ref> Situated about {{convert|17|km|mi|abbr=off}} by road from [[Chennai Zero Point|Chennai]] in the western part of the city, Porur is largely a residential neighbourhood with a significant portion devoted to commercial and industrial activities. Porur's ideal geographic position at the junction of the [[Mount-Poonamallee Road|Mount-Poonamallee]] and Kundrathur roads at the western gates to Chennai city remains a major driver of economic growth.

The earliest [[recorded history]] of Porur goes back to the [[Chola dynasty|Chola period]] when it formed a ''nādu'' of the [[Chola Empire]]. Porur was administered by a village panchayat till 1 October 1977, when it was elevated to the status of a town panchayat. In 2011, the Porur town panchayat was abolished and its jurisdiction included within the [[Greater Chennai Corporation]] as part of the Corporation wards 151 and 153. While traditional in character, Porur has also recently witnessed considerable influx of immigrants from other parts of India largely in connection with industries and services related to the IT, construction and hospitality sectors.

Porur had a population of [[2011 census of India|46,690 in 2011]]. Porur is well-connected by road and has a bus terminus, railway stations and an airport in close proximity. It also has other basic amenities like water supply and sewerage and garbage disposal services, electricity, a sub post office and a police station. Six [[Chennai metro]] stations are being constructed in Porur as part of the Phase II extension activities. The [[Porur Lake]] is one of the biggest lakes in the Chennai metropolitan area and one of the major sources of drinking water to the city while the [[Sri Ramachandra Medical College and Research Institute]], a top-ranked private health sciences university is also situated in Porur.

== Location ==
Porur is located at 13.03° N and 80.16° E, about {{convert|12|km|mi|abbr=off}} west from the Bay of Bengal coast at [[Foreshore Estate]]. It is surrounded by the Chennai neighbourhoods of [[Karambakkam]] and [[Alapakkam]] in the north, [[Valasaravakkam]] and [[Ramapuram, Chennai|Ramapuram]] in the east and [[Mugalivakkam]] to the south and south-east. Westward from Porur on the Mount-Poonamallee Road lie [[Thelliyar Agaram]] and Iyyapanthangal which form part of the [[Mangadu|Mangadu municipality]] of [[Poonamallee taluk]], [[Tiruvallur district]] while on the east, the compound of the Chennai Air Traffic Control Tower Radar Station that extend upto Mugalivakkam Main Road form the limits, the radar station being administered as a part of Mugalivakkam. The shortest distance by road between Porur and Chennai Central Railway Station is {{convert|17|km|mi|abbr=off}}.<ref name="2011census_12a">{{cite web|url=https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s39431c87f273e507e6040fcb07dcb4509/uploads/2018/05/2018050814.pdf|title= Census of India 2011: Tamil Nadu Series-34 Part XII-A District Census Handbook Thiruvallur Village and Town Wise Primary Census Abstract|publisher=Directorate of Census Operations Tamil Nadu}}</ref>

== Geography and climate ==
[[File:Porur Lake and flyover.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Porur Lake]] with the [[Chennai Bypass Road]] bisecting it]]
Porur is situated at an altitude of {{convert|43|m|ft|abbr=off}} above sea level. The soil is primarily alluvial made of clay and silt deposits and highly suited for agricultural activity.<ref name="seismic">{{cite journal|title=Seismic hazard assessment of Chennai city considering local site effects|first1=A.|last1=Boominathan|first2=G. R.|last2=Doddagoudar|first3=A.|last3=Suganthi|first4=R.|last4=Uma Maheswari|url=https://www.ias.ac.in/public/Volumes/jess/117/S2/0853-0863.pdf|work=Journal of Earth System Science|date=November 2008|volume=117|issue=S2|publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref><ref name="toi_20230304">{{cite news|title=How safe is Chennai if an Earthquake Strikes|work=[[Times of India]]|date=2023-03-04|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/how-safe-is-chennai-if-an-earthquake-strikes/articleshow/98402122.cms}}</ref> The Porur Lake is an important source of freshwater for Chennai city though it suffers from encroachment on its banks.<ref name="thehindu_porurlake">{{cite news|title=Porur lake in pitiable state|author=K. Lakshmi|url=http://www.hindu.com/2009/12/20/stories/2009122059630300.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091224104418/http://www.hindu.com/2009/12/20/stories/2009122059630300.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 December 2009|work=[[The Hindu]]|date=20 December 2009}}</ref><ref name="thehindu_20170519">{{cite news|title=Porur Lake has to be fenced|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/chennai/porur-lake-has-to-be-fenced/article18508214.ece|work=The Hindu|first=L.|last=Kanthimathi|date=2017-05-19}}</ref><ref name="thehindu_20120126">{{cite news| last = Lakshmi | first = K. | title = Three tanks set for new lease of life | newspaper = The Hindu | location = Chennai | publisher = The Hindu | date = 2012-01-26 | url = http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/chennai/article2832366.ece | access-date = 31 Jan 2012}}</ref><ref name="thehindu_20131003">{{cite news | last = Lakshmi | first = K. | title = Soon, Porur lake to be cleared of encroachments | newspaper = The Hindu | location = Chennai | publisher = The Hindu | date = 2013-10-03 | url = http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-tamilnadu/soon-porur-lake-to-be-cleared-of-encroachments/article5194750.ece | access-date = 6 Oct 2013}}</ref>
The Porur Lake is connected with the [[Red Hills Lake]] and town of Porur plays an important role in the city's water supply.<ref name="watersupplysanitation">{{cite journal|title=An overview of water supply and sanitation system at metropolitan and peri-urban level: The case of Chennai|url=https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/57a08c97e5274a31e00012f4/R81374.pdf|publisher=Development Planning Unit, University  College, London}}</ref> Low-lying hillocks abutt Porur along the south and south-east, the most prominent among them being the [[Kundrathur Hill|Subramaniyaswami hill of Kundrathur]] and the [[Pallavaram Hill]]. Porur lies on low-to-moderate seismic risk zone the comparatively high water table facilitating liquefaction and absorbing aftershocks.

Under the [[Köppen climate classification]], like the rest of Chennai city, Porur has the dry-summer version of a [[tropical savanna climate]] (''As''),<ref>{{cite book |last1=Elbeltagi |first1=Ahmed |last2=Pande |first2=Chaitanya B. |last3=Moharir |first3=Kanak N. |last4=Pham |first4=Quoc Bao |last5=Singh |first5=Sudhir Kumar |title=Climate Change Impacts on Natural Resources, Ecosystems and Agricultural Systems |date=13 February 2023 |publisher=[[Springer International]] |isbn=978-3-03119-059-9 |page=348}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Khan |first1=Ansar |last2=Akbari |first2=Hashem |last3=Fiorito |first3=Francesco |last4=Mithun |first4=Sk |last5=Niyogi |first5=Dev |title=Global Heat Island Migration |date=2022 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-0-323-85539-6 |page=160 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=P7JYEAAAQBAJ&dq=chennai+dry+summer+climate+As+koppen&pg=PA160}}</ref> During the calendar year 2009, Porur received 1062 mm of rainfall with a maximum temperature of {{cvt|37.6|°C|°F}} and minimum temperature of {{cvt|21.1|°C|°F}} degrees.<ref name="2011census_12a" />

The Porur Lake supports a variety of flora and fauna. Porur is one of the few areas of Chennai where the [[house sparrow]] is found in large numbers with sightings confirmed by the [[Madras Naturalists' Society]] as part of its Sparrow Census project.<ref name="thehindu_20181221">{{cite news|title=Still chirping: Sparrows continue to call Chennai their home|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/chennai/still-chirping-sparrows-continue-to-call-chennai-their-home/article25793300.ece|date=21 December 2018}}</ref><ref name="toi_20181221">{{cite news|title=House sparrows move home, but numbers grow|work=Times of India|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/house-sparrows-move-home-but-numbers-grow/articleshow/67185512.cms|date=21 December 2018}}</ref>

== History ==

The [[Ramanatheswarar Temple, Porur|Ramanatheswarar Temple]] in Porur has an inscription of the Chola king [[Kulothunga I]] who reigned from 1070 CE to 1122 CE.<ref name="inscriptions">{{cite web|title=Arulmigu Ramanadheswarar Temple Porur - Inscriptions|lang=Tamil|publisher=[[Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department]]|url=https://hrce.tn.gov.in/hrcehome/inscription.php?tid=214}}</ref>Porur might have served as the administrative centre of the eponymous ''Perūr Nādū'' of the Chola province of [[Puliyur Kottam]]. The juridisction of Perur Nadu extended over a considerable area and included the surrounding neighbourhoods of [[Manapakkam]] and [[Kolapakkam]] as evidenced by inscriptions at the [[Agasteeswarar Temple, Kolapakkam|Agasteeswarar Temple]] in Kolapakkam.<ref name="sridhar_preface">[[#Sridhar|Sridhar]], pp xvi-xvii</ref><ref name="sridharp37">[[#Sridhar|Sridhar]], p 37</ref>

The earliest modern references to Porur come from British maps and books of the late 18th century. In the early 19th century, the Kodambakkam-Kunrathur road and the St. Thomas Mount-Poonamallee Road were major trade and communication routes leading into Chennai city.<ref name="butterworthp3">[[#Butterworth|Butterworth]], p 3</ref><ref name="butterworthp62">[[#Butterworth|Butterworth]], p 62</ref>However still, Porur was predominantly rural and sparsely populated till the 1960s, when the W. S. Insulators and the Moonlight factory were established with land and support from the Government of Tamil Nadu.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tamil Nadu Government - RTO Details |url=http://www.tn.gov.in/sta/rtocontact.html |website=www.tn.gov.in}}</ref><ref name="ws1p237">{{cite book|title=Indian journal of power and river valley development, Volume 41|pages=237|year=1991}}</ref><ref name="ws2p910">{{cite book|title=Eastern economist, Volume 41|pages=910|year=1963}}</ref><ref name="ws3p">{{cite book|title=India Major Manufacturers|pages=237|publisher=Business Information Agency}}</ref><ref name="madrasgazetteerp805">[[#Baliga|Baliga]], p 805</ref><ref name="madrasgazetteerp870">[[#Baliga|Baliga]], p 870</ref> The population grew from 1,938 in 1961 to 3,539 in 1971 and accelerated even further in the following decades achieving growth rates of 144 percent and 126 percent during 1971-81 and 1981-91 respectively.

The village panchayat administering Porur was upgraded to a Grade-I town panchayat on 1 October 1977.<ref name="madrasgazetteerp1273">[[#Baliga|Baliga]], p 1273</ref> It was further upgraded to a selection grade town panchayat on 24 February 1982.<ref name="madrasgazetteerp1273" />Porur was transferred from the [[Saidapet taluk]] of Chengalpattu district to the [[Ambattur taluk]] of [[Tiruvallur district]] when Chengalpattu district was bifurcated in 1997.<ref name="2011census_12b">{{cite web|url=https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s39431c87f273e507e6040fcb07dcb4509/uploads/2018/05/2018050875-1.pdf|title= Census of India 2011: Tamil Nadu Series-34 Part XII-B District Census Handbook Thiruvallur Village and Town Wise Primary Census Abstract|publisher=Directorate of Census Operations Tamil Nadu}}</ref>The area under the town panchayat was increased from {{convert|3.7|km2|mi2|abbr=on}} to {{convert|5|km2|mi2|abbr=on}}.<ref name="2001_areachange">{{cite web|title=A-4 Appendix 2: Changes in area of towns between 1991-2001 and reasons thereof|url=https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/20049/download/23181/PC01_A04_Appendix2.xls|work=Census 2001 Tables and Publications - Tamil Nadu|publisher=Directorate of Census Operations, Tamil Nadu}}</ref>

On 1 October 2011, the Porur town panchayat was dissolved and the areas under its jurisdiction absorbed into the [[Greater Chennai Corporation]] where they were distributed between wards 151 and 153 of the corporation.<ref name="toi_20110114">{{cite news|title=Bill to expand Chennai passed by T. N. Assembly|work=Times of India|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/bill-to-expand-chennai-passed-by-tn-assembly/articleshow/7279915.cms|date=14 January 2011}}</ref><ref name="bill2_2011">{{cite web|title=L. A. Bill No. 2 of 2011 A Bills further to amend the Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919|url=https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_states/tamil-nadu/2011/Bill2of2011TN.pdf|work=Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary|year=2011}}</ref><ref name="tngazette_2018">{{cite web|title=No. VI(2)/160(a-3)/2018|work=Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary|url=https://chennaicorporation.gov.in/gcc/delimited_ward/pdf/2018_delimitation.pdf|publisher=Government of Tamil Nadu}}</ref><ref name="cmda_masterplan">{{cite web|title=Abstract of areas added to Chennai metropolitan area|url=https://www.cmdachennai.gov.in/pdfs/masterplan.pdf|publisher=[[Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority]]}}</ref>In 2018, Porur was transferred from Tiruvallur district to [[Chennai district]] where it forms part of the [[Maduravoyal taluk]].<ref name="go1_2018">{{cite web|title=G. O. (Ms.) No. 1|url=https://cla.tn.gov.in/documents/government-orders/GO_No_01_04-01-2018.pdf|date=2018-01-04|publisher=Government of Tamil Nadu}}</ref>

According to the 2011 India [[census]], Porur had a population of 46,690 with men constituting 23,450 (50.22%) and women constituting 23,250 (49.79%) with a sex ratio of 991.<ref name="porur_limits">While the townships of [[Thelliyar Agaram]] (presently part of the Mangadu municipality of Kanchipuram district), [[Karambakkam]] (now Ward No. 150 of the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC)), [[Alapakkam]] (Ward No. 146 and portion of Ward No. 147 of GCC)  and [[Mugalivakkam]] (Ward No. 156 of GCC) can be considered more-or-less suburbs of Porur, to avoid ambiguity, only the 2011 census details for the town panchayat of Porur are provided</ref><ref name="2011census_12b" /><ref name="2011census_12a" />The adult [[literacy]] rate was 93.66% with a male literacy rate of 96.5% and a female literacy rate of 90.80%.<ref name="2011census_12a" />The total number of households was 11,803.<ref name="2011census_12b" /> The population of scheduled castes was 3,647 and scheduled tribes, 49.<ref name="2011census_12a" />There were 5,112 children who were under 6 years of age.<ref name="2011census_12a" />There were 564 cultivators and 209 agricultural labourers.<ref name="2011census_12b" />There were three notified slums within the Porur town panchayat with a population of 6,300.<ref name="2011census_12b" /> They were Kaliamman Koil, Thiruveethi Amman Koil and Chinna Porur. Slum dwellers constituted 13.49 percent of the total population of Porur.<ref name="2011census_12a" />

As per the 2011 census, Hindus formed the majority numbering 39,394 individuals making up 84.37 percent of the total population followed by the Christians who numbered 3,956 (8.47% of the population) and Muslims who were 1,615 (3.45%).<ref name="2011census_religion">{{cite web|title=Census Tables C-01 Population by religious community|publisher=Census of India|url=https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/11392/download/14505/DDW33C-01%20MDDS.XLS}}</ref> There were also 71 Jains, 27 Sikhs and 16 Buddhists.<ref name="2011census_religion" />The Ramanathaswamy and Balamurugan temples of Porur attest to a Hindu presence stretching back over a thousand years. Porur has a significant and active Christian population due to Christian missionary work in Porur's Harijan colonies before and after independence.

The most widely spoken first language as per the 2011 census was [[Tamil language|Tamil]] spoken by 39,948 people (85.56% of the population). [[Telugu language|Telugu]] was spoken by 3,681 people (7.88%), [[Malayalam]] - 1,250 (2.67%), [[Hindi]] - 538 (1.09%), [[Urdu]] - 510 (1.09%), Kannada - 228 (0.4%), Marathi - 160 (0.34%) and Saurashtri - 108 (0.3%).<ref name="2011census_mothertongue">{{cite web|title=C-16 City: Population by mother tongue (town level), Tamil Nadu - 2011|url=https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/10259/download/13371/DDW-C16-TOWN-STMT-MDDS-3300.XLSX|publisher=Census of India}}</ref> The native language of Porur is Tamil which was the mother tongue for as much as 96.7 percent of the population in 1951. Inter-state migration in search of job opportunities in the information technology, construction and hospitality industry have resulted in an increase of people speaking languages other than Tamil from 3.3 percent in 1951 to 14.44 percent in 2011 with the Telugu-speaking population rising from 3.2 percent in 1951 to 7.88 percent in 2011 and those of other languages from 0.1 percent in 1951 to 6.56 percent in 2011.

Prior to 1 October 2011, Porur was administered by a [[town panchayat]] headed by a President assisted by 18 councillors. The executive powers were vested in an Executive Officer who was usually an officer of the Tamil Nadu State civil service. Since its inclusion in the Greater Chennai Corporation, the territory under the defunct Porur town panchayat was distributed between the wards 151 and 153 of the Greater Chennai Corporation represented by an elected councillor each for the two wards.<ref name="tngazette_2018" /> Both the wards come under the Zone No. 11 (Valasaravakkam) of the Greater Chennai Corporation.<ref name="go_wardsdelimitation">{{cite web|title=G. O. (Ms.) No. 136 dt 12-9-2011|url=http://www.tniuscbe.org/download/go/go1123.pdf|publisher=Government of Tamil Nadu}}</ref>The area administered by the Porur town panchayat at the time of its dissolution in 2011 was {{convert|5|km2|mi2|abbr=on}} and excluded [[Thelliyar Agaram]], [[Karambakkam]], [[Alapakkam]] and [[Mugalivakkam]] while its income during the year 1989-90 was Rs. 35.41 lakhs.<ref name="gazetteer2000p1362">{{cite book|title=Gazetteers of India Tamil Nadu: Kancheepuram and Tiruvallur Districts|volume=2|page=1362|year=2000|first=M.|last=Gopalakrishnan|publisher=Government of Tamil Nadu}}</ref>

Porur forms part of the [[Maduravoyal Assembly constituency]] of the [[Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly]] and [[Sriperumbudur Lok Sabha constituency]] of the [[Parliament of India]].<ref name="delimitationcommission">{{cite web|title=Order No. 43|date=2007-04-05|page=6|url=https://www.eci.gov.in/eci-backend/public/api/download?url=LMAhAK6sOPBp%252FNFF0iRfXbEB1EVSLT41NNLRjYNJJP1KivrUxbfqkDatmHy12e%252FzVx8fLfn2ReU7TfrqYobgItkbtjWZ5zoNxbsk2AET34bEBjqhsqFaGWEo4eNwAACFYwZvSyMmByYKzu9WfwbyqMOF2Fs7aTXHpCOyKKdx%252FUZ%252Fy5nKA3GDyWJOLBYKRnGa#:~:text=TO%20BE%20PUBLISHED%20IN%20EXTRAORDINARY,ASSEMBLY%20CONSTITUENCIES%20AND%20THEIR%20EXTENT}}</ref> The incumbent member of the Tamil Nadu legislature is [[P. Rhevanth Charan]] of the [[Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam]] while the incumbent member of the Lok Sabha is [[T. R. Baalu]] of the [[Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam]].<ref name="Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly election Result  2026 - Maduravoyal" />

Porur has many ancient Hindu temples like the Ramanatheswarar Temple that dates from the Chola period. There are also temples that have constructed quite recently. The [[Sethu Kshetram]] temple was constructed in 1964 for the employees of W. S. Insulators and inaugurated by the Shankaracharya of Sringeri. A tree was planted during the ''kumbabhishekam'' of the shrine on 27 October 1966 by [[R. Venkataraman]], Minister of Industries for the Government of Madras. The Ramanatheswarar Temple and Balamurugan Temple are managed by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department of the Government of Tamil Nadu.

Water supply is provided by the Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board with headworks at Chinna Porur and Mount-Poonamallee Road while electricity is provided by the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited. Law and order enforcement is handled by the T-15 SRMC police station which comes under the jurisdiction of the [[Avadi Police|Avadi police comissionerate]]. The nearest fire station is located at [[Kumananchavadi]].<ref name="2011census_12a" />

Porur has two public parks, one each for the wards 151 and 153, maintained by the Greater Chennai Corporation. The [[Dr. M. S. Swaminathan Wetland Eco Park]] was established in Porur at a cost of Rs. 20 crores and inaugurated by the [[Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu]], [[M. K. Stalin]] on 7 March 2025.<ref name="indianexpress">{{cite news|title=CM Stalin opens Swaminathan Wetland Park|url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/tamil-nadu/2025/Mar/08/cm-stalin-opens-swaminathan-wetland-park|work=[[Indian Express]]|date=8 March 2025}}</ref><ref name="thehindu_ecopark">{{cite news|title=Porur eco park in Chennai is a space for nature, play, wellness|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/chennai/the-porur-eco-park-is-a-space-for-nature-play-and-wellness/article69391112.ece|date=7 April 2025|first=Geetha|last=Srimathi|work=The Hindu}}</ref>

== Economy ==
[[File:PorurSaravanaStores.jpg|thumb|left|Saravana Stores outlet in Porur, 2022]]
Traditionally, Porur, like many of its surrounding villages, had an agrarian economy. The settlement grew around the two temples dedicated to Ramanathaswamy and Balamurugan and the Porur market in the vicinity serving as the town's chief marketplace. Surrounding the settlement on all sides were agricultural lands with rice being the chief crop. At the turn of the 20th century, the agricultural workers of Porur had organised themselves into a second-class cooperative society which was making a profit of Rs. 107-5-9 in 1905.<ref name="report_coop">{{cite book|title=Annual Report on the Working of Co-operative Societies|page=17|year=1905|publisher=Cooperative Department, Government of Madras}}</ref> With the expansion of the nearby city of Madras in the years following independence, corporates began setting up their offices in Porur. The first was the construction company [[Larsen & Toubro]] whose city offices were opened at [[Manapakkam]] near Porur followed by the cosmetic brand [[T. S. R. & Co]] at [[Ramapuram, Chennai|Ramapuram]]. The [[W. S. Industries (India)]], Rainbow Inks and Varnishes, the Norton Plastics and Film Company and S. & S. Power Switchgear Ltd along the Mount-Poonamallee Road and the Moonlight factory at Ramapuram were set up in the 1960s.<ref name="researchp381">{{cite book|title=Research and Industry|volume=8|page=381|year=1963|publisher=Council for Scientific and Industrial Rsearch}}</ref> The W. S. Industries (India) manufactured high tension and low tension insulators, lightning arrestors, condenser bushings, transformers, regulators, switchgear and switches in collaboration with [[Westinghouse Electric Corporation]] with a declared production capacity of 2,400 tons per annum in 1964.<ref name="researchp381" />Until the end of the 20th century, Porur's chief manufactures were transformers while its exports were fruits and garments.<ref name="1991pca_chengalpattu">{{cite web|title=Census of India 1991 Series-23 Tamil Nadu District Census Handbook Chengalpattu M. G. R. District Part XII-A|url=https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/45414/download/49624/1991_DCHB_Chengalpattu_Part_A.pdf|publisher=Government of India}}</ref> By 2011, with W. S. Industries (India) having closed down, readymade garments and footwear had replaced transformers as the town's chief items of manufacture.<ref name="2011census_12a" />

During the information technology boom of the 1990s, Larsen & Toubro started its own software and software enabled services subsidiary [[LTIMindtree|L&T Infotech]] at Manapakkam followed by the The Arcot Road and Mount-Poonamallee Road stretches remain the shopping and entertainment hubs of Porur with major banks, retail garments and jewellery stores and restaurant chains operating branches and retail outlets. [[Saravana Stores]] opened its Porur outlet in Sakthi Nagar with heavy publicity on 7 December 2017.<ref name="sarvanastores_inauguration">{{cite web|title=Saravana Stores Porur inauguration video|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PpLb6vIzQnA}}</ref>

== Education and healthcare ==

As of 2009, there were a total of 14 primary schools, 12 middle schools, 11 secondary and senior secondary schools in Porur.<ref name="2011census_12a" />There was a polytechnic institute, the Little Flower Polytechnic College, in Porur while the nearest arts, science and engineering colleges were situated in Chennai city.<ref name="2011census_12a" />There were a total pf 8 recognised vocational training institutes while the nearest school for the disabled was situated at Poonamallee, about {{convert|7|km|mi|abbr=off}} away.<ref name="2011census_12a" />There was also a hospital, a dispensary, a family welfare clinic, a maternity and child welfare centre, a  maternity home and a veterinary hospital within Porur town panchayat limits besides a charitable hospital cum nursing home and around 20 medical shops.<ref name="2011census_12a" /> The nearest dental college is the SRM Dental College in Ramapuram.<ref name="srmdentalcollege">{{cite web|title=About US|url=https://srmdentalcollege.ac.in/about-srm/|publisher=SRM Dental College}}</ref>

The Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research, established in 1985, is frequently rated among the best medical colleges and healthcare institutions in India. While traditionally a part of Porur, the college is administered as a part of Thelliyar Agaram which in turn forms a part of the municipality of [[Mangadu]] in [[Kancheepuram district]]. The college offers postgraduate courses in all medical subjects besides doctoral courses in [[Neurosurgery]], [[Surgical oncology]], [[Cardiac surgery|Cardiac Surgery]] and [[Doctorate of Medicine|DM]] in [[Cardiology]], [[Neurology]] etc. The [[National Institutional Ranking Framework]] (NIRF) ranked Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research 96 overall in India in 2024, 10th in Dental Category, 55 among universities, 20 in the medical ranking, and 31 in the pharmacy ranking.<ref name="nirf_2024">{{Cite web |title=NIRF Ranking 2024 |url=https://www.nirfindia.org/nirfpdfcdn/2024/pdf/Report/IR2024_Report.pdf}}</ref> It was ranked first among private health science university in India in 2022 by ''[[India Today]]''.<ref name=Rankings_IT_M_2020>{{cite news|title=India Today Top 20 college rankings for 2020|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/bestcolleges/2020/ranks/1824931|work=India Today|year=2020}}</ref>The Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research had a total of 5,138 undergraduate and 1,475 post-graduate students on its rolls during the academic year 2018-19.<ref name=UGC>{{cite web |title=Deemed Universities |url=https://www.ugc.ac.in/deemeduniversitylist.aspx?id=31&Unitype=4 |publisher=[[University Grants Commission (India)|University Grants Commission]] |access-date=21 March 2019}}</ref>

== Transport and communication ==
[[Image:Porur Junction.jpg|thumb|right|200 px|Porur Junction in 2011]]
Porur is well connected by road to the rest of Chennai city. The [[Mount-Poonamallee Road]] that runs between [[Poonamallee]] and [[Kathipara Junction]] is a [[State highways in India|State Highway]] that connects Porur with the [[Grand Southern Trunk Road]]. Beyond Poonamallee, the Mount-Poonamallee Road links with the [[National Highway 4 (India, old numbering)]] to [[Bengaluru]]. The [[Porur Junction]] is an extremely busy traffic intersection in Porur where the major arterial roads meet.<ref name="thehindu_20231120">{{cite news|title=Travel between Porur and Arcot Road is frustrating for commuters|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/chennai/travel-between-porur-and-arcot-road-is-frustrating-for-commuters/article67295669.ece|first1=Geetha|last1=Srimath|first2=Sunitha|last2=Sekar|date=2023-11-02}}</ref><ref name="thehindu_20150221">{{cite news|title=Mayhem at Porur junction|url=https://www.thehindu.com/features/downtown/mayhem-at-porur-junction/article6920053.ece|work=The Hindu|first=K.|last=Sarumathi|date=2015-02-21}}</ref><ref name="thehindu_20240311">{{cite news|title=Wider and better roads needed at Porur to handle burgeoning traffic|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/chennai/wider-and-better-roads-needed-at-porur-to-handle-burgeoning-traffic/article67933425.ece|work=The Hindu|date=2024-03-11|first=K.|last=Lakshmi}}</ref>The [[Arcot Road]] connects Porur Junction with [[Kodambakkam]] while the Kundrathur Road links Porur Junction with [[Kundrathur]]. Porur had a total of {{convert|37|km|mi|abbr=off}} of roads in 2011.<ref name="2011census_12b" />

Porur is served by an efficient public transportation system. The nearest MTC bus terminus is situated at [[Iyyappanthangal]]. There are bus services linking Porur with [[Royapuram]], [[Island Grounds]], [[Saidapet]], [[Little Mount, Chennai|Little Mount]], [[T. Nagar]], [[Thiruvanmiyur]], [[Mandaveli]], [[Nanganallur]], [[Mugalivakkam]], [[Ramapuram, Chennai|Ramapuram]], Poonamallee, [[Vellavedu]] and [[Sriperumbudur]] through the Mount-Poonamallee Road and  Kundrathur, [[Pattur]], [[Mangadu]] through the Kundrathur Road and Porur Junction with Royapuram, [[Vadapalani]], [[K. K. Nagar, Chennai|K. K. Nagar]], [[Vallalar Nagar]] and [[M. K. B. Nagar]] through Arcot Road.<ref name="mtc_stagewiseinfo">{{cite web|title=Routes passing through stages|url=https://mtcbus.tn.gov.in/Home/stagewiseinfo|publisher=Metropolitan Transport Corporation (Chennai) Ltd}}</ref>There are seven major bus stops: Saravana Stores/Sakthi Nagar, Gopalakrishna theatre, Porur Junction and Sri Ramachandra Medical College on the Mount-Poonamallee Road and Lakshmi Nagar, Alapakkam and Karambakkam on Arcot Road. There are private bus and share auto services from Porur Junction to Guindy and small bus services providing connectivity from Porur Junction to the [[Alandur metro station]] (Route S84) and Porur Junction to Guindy TVK Estate bus stop (Route S27).<ref name="cmrl_lastmile">{{cite web|title=Metro connect (Feeder service)|url=https://chennaimetrorail.org/feeder-service/|publisher=Chennai Metro Rail Limited}}</ref><ref name="routes84">{{cite web|title=Route S84 CMRL Minibus|url=https://chennaimetrorail.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/s84-TENTATIVE.pdf|publisher=Chennai Metro Rail Limited}}</ref><ref name="routes27">{{cite web|title=Route S27|url=https://mtcbus.tn.gov.in/Home/routewiseinfo?csrf_test_name=c4b3203e13377da82bc2ee9022abe5dc&selroute=S27&submit=|publisher=Metropolitan Transport Corporation (Chennai) Limited}}</ref>The nearest suburban railway station is [[Guindy railway station|Guindy]] ({{convert|8|km|mi|abbr=off}}) while the nearest domestic-cum-international airport is located at [[Meenambakkam]].<ref name="2011census_12a" />

The [[Porur Junction metro station]], [[Porur Bypass metro station]], [[Karambakkam metro station]], [[Thelliyaragaram metro station]] and [[Alapakkam metro station]] are under construction along the [[Line 4 (Chennai Metro)|Yellow Line]] while the [[Mugalivakkam metro station]] is being built on the [[Line 5 (Chennai Metro)|Red Line]] of the [[Chennai Metro]].<ref name="phaseIImap">{{cite web|title=Phase II Route Map|url=https://chennaimetrorail.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Phase-II-Map-Updated-Map-PHASE-2.pdf|publisher=Chennai Metro Rail Limited}}</ref> The [[Alandur metro station]] is the nearest operational metro station.

Porur has a [[sub post office]] of [[India Post]] in Sakthi Nagar which falls under the Avadi Camp Sub Division of the Tambaram Division of Chennai City Region, Tamil Nadu Circle.<ref name="headpo">{{cite web|title=Lit of Head Post Offices|url=https://tamilnadupost.cept.gov.in/hpos.php|publisher=Tamil Nadu Postal Circle}}</ref><ref name="locatepo_pincode">{{cite web|title=Locate post office by pin code - 600116|url=https://www.indiapost.gov.in/post-office-details?pincode=600116|publisher=India Post}}</ref> Apart from Sakthi Nagar, there are also sub post offices in Alapakkam and Sri Ramachandra Deemed University campus.<ref name="locatepo_pincode" />Regular postal services including speed post and parcel are provided along with postal savings and deposit accounts, postal insurance, etc.

extract:
Porur (Tamil: [poːɾuːɾ]) is a neighbourhood of the city of Chennai, India. It forms part of the Maduravoyal taluk of Chennai district. Situated about 17 kilometres (11 miles) by road from Chennai in the western part of the city, Porur is largely a residential neighbourhood with a significant portion devoted to commercial and industrial activities. Porur's ideal geographic position at the junction of the Mount-Poonamallee and Kundrathur roads at the western gates to Chennai city remains a major driver of economic growth.
The earliest recorded history of Porur goes back to the Chola period when it formed a nādu of the Chola Empire. Porur was administered by a village panchayat till 1 October 1977, when it was elevated to the status of a town panchayat. In 2011, the Porur town panchayat was abolished and its jurisdiction included within the Greater Chennai Corporation as part of the Corporation wards 151 and 153. While traditional in character, Porur has also recently witnessed considerable influx of immigrants from other parts of India largely in connection with industries and services related to the IT, construction and hospitality sectors.
Porur had a population of 46,690 in 2011. Porur is well-connected by road and has a bus terminus, railway stations and an airport in close proximity. It also has other basic amenities like water supply and sewerage and garbage disposal services, electricity, a sub post office and a police station. Six Chennai metro stations are being constructed in Porur as part of the Phase II extension activities. The Porur Lake is one of the biggest lakes in the Chennai metropolitan area and one of the major sources of drinking water to the city while the Sri Ramachandra Medical College and Research Institute, a top-ranked private health sciences university is also situated in Porur.
